newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-MALI'S YOUNGSTERS FACE CHARACTER TEST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MALI'S YOUNGSTERS FACE CHARACTER TEST.

text.p: The bold youth policy of west Africans Mali faces its toughest test yet this weekend against neighbours Ivory Coast in the African Nations' Cup qualifiers.
Mali play the Ivorians in Bamako on Sunday in one of 12 qualifiers set for the continent this week.
Particular focus will be on the youthful Malian team, put together by coach and former national team goalkeeper Mamadou Keita, in their group two game.
Keita led Mali to the semifinals of the 1994 Nations' Cup in Tunisia but disbanded his team after they failed to qualify for the last finals in South Africa last year.
He has since set out on a deliberate policy to blood many of the teenage talents in the arrid west African country and expose the young footballers to the rigours of international competition.
Last year Mali's youngsters struggled in friendly internationals in Africa and then on tour in the Middle East but the team have won their opening two Nations' Cup qualifiers.
Mali scored a 2-1 away win over Benin in October but really surprised by beating Algeria 1-0 at home last month.
"We are still in the process of building the team for the future," said Keita.
"That's why we didn't enter the World Cup. We thought two qualifying tournaments would be too much and that they are not yet ready for the big time."
Victory over perennial rivals Ivory Coast would propel Mali further ahead at the top of the standings and seemingly turn their boys into men.

Ethiopia, who meet Egypt in Addis Ababa on Sunday in their group three game, will be watching Malian progress with interest as they try to pick up the pieces after the mass defection of players last month.
A total of 16 squad members defected in Italy while travelling from the Ethiopian capital to Morocco for a Nations' Cup qualifier last month.
Ethiopia were granted a postponement of that match and have decided to go ahead with participation in the qualifiers but will be major underdogs even at home.
One consolation for them will be the absence of Egypt's up-and-coming striker Aly Maher, suspended after being sent off against Senegal last month.
He is just one of several leading African footballers not expected to feature in this weekend's encounters.

Zimbabwean officials say they are not confident that goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar, standing trial on match fixing charges in Britain, will be allowed to travel for the key group one encounter against Angola in Harare on Sunday.
"Now that the trial is close to finishing we don't know if the judge will let him leave the country," said coach Ian Porterfield.
But Zimbabwe will have another Englsh-based player, Peter Ndlovu of Coventry, back after a long injury-enforced absence.
Guinea, who host Sierra Leone in group four, will be without French-based strker Abdoubacar "Titi" Camara. Last month he said he was retiring from international soccer.

Former World Footballer of the Year George Weah is unlikely to join his Liberian compatriots for their trip to Tanzania in group six. Liberia lost their qualifying match against Togo last month without the AC Milan striker.
